data.title: Nummular (discoid) eczema — viva
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Nummular (discoid) eczema** (Eczemas)_

**Q1. What is nummular eczema?**
- Chronic eczema with coin-shaped (nummular) well-demarcated plaques, very itchy
- Two age peaks: young women (15–25) and elderly men (50–65); also in atopic children

**Q2. Morphology.**
- Starts as tiny papulovesicles that coalesce into round plaques 1–10 cm, oozing and crusting in acute stage, scaly and lichenified later; may show central clearing (mimicking tinea)
- Sites: legs and dorsa of hands and feet, extensor forearms, trunk

**Q3. Aetiological associations.**
- Xerosis and barrier damage, atopy, S. aureus colonisation (infective eczema), contact allergy (nickel, chromate, fragrances, neomycin), venous stasis, alcohol, drugs (isotretinoin, interferon, TNF inhibitors), dental/focal infection (older theory)

**Q4. Differential diagnosis.**
- Tinea corporis (active edge, KOH), psoriasis (silvery scale, nails, other sites), impetigo, Bowen's disease (single, slowly growing), mycosis fungoides, granuloma annulare, contact dermatitis, lichen simplex

**Q5. What is infective (infectious eczematoid) dermatitis? (PYQ)**
- Eczema around a discharging infected focus (otitis externa, ulcer, fistula) from exudate; spreads peripherally; treat infection + steroid
- Significance of bacteria in eczema — S. aureus colonises >90% of AD lesions; superantigens drive inflammation and steroid resistance

**Q6. Investigations.**
- KOH, swab culture, patch test (especially if refractory), biopsy if atypical, blood sugar

**Q7. Treatment.**
- Emollients, potent topical steroid (ointment) ± occlusion; combined steroid–antibiotic for short term when infected; oral antibiotics (cephalexin, cloxacillin) for widespread infected lesions
- Tacrolimus, coal tar, NB-UVB, systemic agents (methotrexate, cyclosporine) for widespread resistant disease; sedating antihistamines
- Treat xerosis, stop alcohol

**Q8. Prognosis?**
- Chronic and relapsing; often recurs at previous sites

**Q9. What does dermoscopy show?**
- Dotted vessels in a patchy distribution with yellow crusts/ serocrusts and white scales — compared with psoriasis (uniform dotted vessels with white scales on a red background)

**Q10. Role of patch testing.**
- Contact sensitisation (nickel, chromate, cobalt, fragrance, neomycin, preservatives in emollients) found in up to a third of chronic nummular eczema — patch test when persistent or atypical distribution (e.g. hands, feet, lower legs)

## Quick spotter facts
- Coin-shaped oozing itchy plaques on legs — nummular eczema; do KOH to exclude tinea

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Eczemas). Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
